answer:
Keep the two core segments as two separately-identified specimens and add the new stratigraphic correlation as an extra, additive assertion between them -- do not retro-fit them into a single E19/S13 instance. CRMsci's own scope notes for S11 Amount of Matter and S13 Sample already anticipate this exact geology case: they name 'the sequence of layers of a bore core' as the kind of thing an Amount of Matter's identity rests on, and note that a sample 'ceases to exist' when that layering is corrupted -- i.e. the CRM treats a bore core's continuity as a fact about the rock, not a licence to collapse two administratively distinct catalogue entries into one. Each segment should stay typed as its own S13 Sample (subclass of S11 Amount of Matter / S10 Material Substantial, and of E18 Physical Thing via E19 Physical Object), each keeping its own P48 has preferred identifier / P1 is identified by pointing at its own E42 Identifier (the accession number), established by its own past E15 Identifier Assignment. Nothing about the new geological finding requires touching those -- an object can carry more than one identifier over its life, and the fifty years of loan paperwork is simply documentation created while each specimen was correctly known only by its own number; it stays true of that specimen regardless of what is asserted about it later.

The strongest direct precedent I found is Martin Doerr's own ship-of-Theseus discussion in thread t1170 (Issue 369, discussing E19 identity): pieces stored separately for a century and later technically rejoined are proposed to be treated as a NEW E19 object, 'because the continuity of functionality is broken' -- his test for Amount-of-Matter identity is explicitly whether there is 'original matter in it which can provide evidence of its original/initial states', which is a question you can now answer 'yes' to about the correlation, without it forcing the two catalogued specimens back into one thing. By the same logic, these two core segments were split into separate custody, separate accession series and separate documentation from the moment each was drilled and boxed; recognizing decades later that the rock is stratigraphically continuous is new evidence about the geology, not grounds for merging two persistent, separately-administered specimens whose identity was already fixed by that administrative act.

For the 'documented physical relationship' itself, `connect S13 S13` / `connect E19 E19` surface P130 shows features of (features are also found on) as the only property built for exactly this shape of claim: a directed-or-symmetric link between two things sharing diagnostic features without necessarily one causing the other, and its own scope note calls out 'siblings of a derivation process from a common source' as a case it is meant for -- which is precisely what two segments of the same original stratum, recovered through separate drilling events, are. I would assert P130 between the two S13 Sample instances (or, if a scope note field is wanted, note the shared source formation as the common cause) and record the stratigrapher's re-identification as a new E13 Attribute Assignment / E17 Type Assignment-style event layered on top, not as a change to either specimen's own identity or identifiers.

rejected_alternatives.option: Merge the two accessioned segments into one E19/S13 instance with a single identity
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Thread t1170 (Martin Doerr, Issue 369) treats the analogous case -- pieces separated for decades then rejoined -- as a NEW object precisely because continuity was broken in the interim; E19/S13 identity in this archive is anchored to the administrative act of accessioning, not retroactively revisable once fifty years of loan documentation already treats them as two things.

rejected_alternatives.option: O25 contains (is contained in), S10 -> S10
rejected_alternatives.why_not: `connect S13 S13` and `connect S11 S11` both offer it, but it expresses one Material Substantial currently containing another; neither core segment contains the other -- they are two disjoint amounts of matter recovered from different boreholes, not a part-in-place relationship.

rejected_alternatives.option: P46 is composed of, E18 -> E18
rejected_alternatives.why_not: `connect E19 E19` offers it, but it asserts a synchronic whole made of coexisting parts. The two segments were never documented as one whole to begin with, and nothing proposes physically rejoining them -- only that they were once continuous before drilling and burial history separated them.

rejected_alternatives.option: L54 is same as, E1 -> E1 (CRMdig)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Offered by `connect S13 S13` as a 'non-unique identification' link, but it belongs to CRMdig (digital-provenance coreference between representations) and has only one raw mention in the whole archive with no thread discussing physical-specimen use; P130's scope note is a closer, better-attested fit for this case's 'siblings from a common source' pattern.
